Parse plain decimal numbers to the correctly rounded double

Source: R/io_utils.R
dot-parse_decimal.Rd

Python's float() returns the double nearest the decimal, and neither of R's own parsers does in every case: measured over 200,000 random decimals, readr's parse_double() missed by one unit in the last place on 26,706 and as.numeric() on 35, among them 0.586135918132 and 2.91e-11. A value with at most 15 significant digits and a power of ten within 10^22 is therefore computed as one exact integer times or divided by one exact power of ten. That is a single IEEE-754 operation, which is correctly rounded, so both engines reach the same double. Every value in the shipped lexica is of that kind. Any other value is rounded by exact integer arithmetic (.decimal_to_double()). as.numeric() is not used there, because it accumulates the digits in long double. Where that type is wider than a double, as on x86-64, it missed the nearest double on 25 of 60,008 such values. Where it is no wider, as on Apple Silicon, it misses far more often. R CMD check on macOS read 0.12345678901234567 one unit away, and an emulation of the parser in double precision missed on about one in ten of the values Python's repr() writes for computed doubles. readr's parser missed on 21,644 of the 60,008, and it read 1e400 as 1e307 and 1e-400 as 1e-307, where float() gives Inf and 0. A negative zero is read as zero, because the two engines' writers would print it as -0 and 0.

Usage

.parse_decimal(x)

Arguments

x

A character vector whose non-missing values match .NUMERIC_CELL.

Value

A double vector.
